Topic: COVID-19 Impact on Health Services

Clues (max 200 words): “Movement of people in and out of the country has minimized, business is not running as usual because people don’t go out to buy goods so as a result the prices of goods is rising.” “People always grumbling that things were hard, things were hard.” “The only thing, the influx of patients at the initial stage of the outbreak, drop. This was because people were afraid to come to the health facility.” “Drugs in our facility are really scanty now.” “Most of the drugs are not coming as they used to.”

Reasoning (max 150 words): The respondent details systemic challenges faced by health services due to COVID-19, including reduced movement and economic slowdown, which have led to increased prices (Clue 2). Fear of visiting health facilities has resulted in a significant drop in patient influx (Clue 3), compounded by drug shortages (Clue 5). These interconnected issues highlight the severe impact of COVID-19 on health service delivery, limiting patient access and increasing difficulties for health workers.

Topic: Staffing and Training Adaptations during COVID-19

Clues (max 200 words): “The change that took place is a positive change because it got added.” “I think it is a positive change.” “I have two workers there, that I’m supervising.” “There is no negative change in the staffing. We are still the same staff.” “But if they find out that there is medicine at the facility, they will come because they believe that the government drugs are better than those on the street.” “my role just as I said, is many... I am the IPC vocal again... I have gone through all these training and I have to pass it on to my colleagues.” “...training come by batches, not a general training per say. Maybe they will say on EPI.”

Reasoning (max 150 words): The respondent describes an increase in responsibilities and adaptations in training protocols due to COVID-19. While staffing levels remained stable, the individual's supervisory and mentorship roles have expanded, reflecting a positive change (Clue 1 and Clue 2). The shift to batch training illustrates a focused approach to ensure health workers are equipped to handle the pandemic while managing their regular duties (Clue 6). This indicates adaptability and a commitment to enhancing the workforce's capacity in response to the ongoing health crisis.

Topic: Supply Chain Issues and Drug Availability

Clues (max 200 words): “Drugs in our facility are really scanty now.” “The ACT, they supplied for adolescent and adult which is not enough.” “Even the one they gave is the 90, 90 and even the 90 pieces if we use it on the number of patients today it will finish.” “I included cotton wool, blood syrup and all that is lacking.” “Even these are not available.” “most of the drugs are not coming as they used to.” “the only thing I received was only on malaria treatment: few ACTs.”

Reasoning (max 150 words): The respondent highlights critical supply chain issues, especially concerning drug availability (Clue 1). Insufficient quantities of essential medications, such as ACT (Clue 2) and other medical supplies, underscore systemic problems that hinder the facility's capacity to serve patients effectively. The repeated emphasis on shortages and scant supplies indicates a critical gap in the healthcare system, worsened by the pandemic, which poses risks to patient care and overall public health.

Topic: Psychological Impact and Morale of Health Workers

Clues (max 200 words): “that creates fear among us because if your colleague is having the face mask and you are not wearing one.” “these are some of the things that are lacking at our facility. Things that we’ll really want to have to help bust up our morals to work.” “the support that am aware of, is the one which came in the form of health talk or health sensitization.” “if you see someone with gloves, then only he knows how he got it.” “the only comment that I will give is that I am not the [retracted]. So whatever comment I give is based on my own understanding.”

Reasoning (max 150 words): The clues reflect the psychological strain and morale issues faced by health workers during the pandemic. The fear of infection due to inadequate personal protective equipment (PPE) exacerbates staff anxiety (Clue 1). The absence of adequate support measures highlights an urgent need for institutional backing to boost morale (Clue 2). The mention of limited health talks as the only form of support indicates insufficient resources to address mental health concerns, emphasizing the importance of psychological well-being in maintaining a resilient healthcare workforce.

Topic: Public Perception and Trust in Health Services

Clues (max 200 words): “patients were afraid to come to the health facility.” “if they believe that the government drugs are better than those on the street.” “some people say ‘even if I go to the health facility, there will be no drugs, then why can’t I go and buy drugs from the pharmacy.’” “they see it as, in fact most people take it to be a common cold.” “the fear was there compared to now.”

Reasoning (max 150 words): The clues underscore the significant role of public perception in health service utilization during the COVID-19 pandemic. The fear of visiting health facilities (Clue 1) indicates a breakdown of trust in the system, leading patients to seek alternatives (Clue 3). While there is some confidence in government resources (Clue 2), skepticism remains, compounded by a perception of COVID-19 as less severe (Clue 4). This shifting dynamic in public sentiment poses challenges for health services in fostering trust and encouraging appropriate healthcare-seeking behaviors.

Topic: Comparison of COVID-19 and Ebola Response

Clues (max 200 words): “During Ebola we were fortunate to have more drugs compared to this covid.” “With covid, availability of drug is a big problem.” “The death rate during Ebola was so high compared to covid-19.” “Even during Ebola, it was more fearful to me than this covid-19.” “the restriction of movement has really helped to a certain extent...the problem was with identifying an infected person.” 

Reasoning (max 150 words): The clues provide a comparative analysis of responses to the Ebola outbreak and the COVID-19 pandemic. The respondent notes that drug availability was better during Ebola (Clue 1), highlighting weaknesses in the current system regarding COVID-19 (Clue 2). The higher death rates during Ebola contributed to greater public fear (Clue 3), while perceptions of COVID-19 have shifted to being less severe (Clue 4). The insights suggest that lessons from Ebola could inform improvements in current health crisis strategies.

You will find out that even before the outbreak in Sierra Leone, we and the government, that restriction on the international boarders was the reason for the long time it took for us to get the covid outbreak."

Reasoning (max 150 words): The clues emphasize critical issues in drug availability and overall health system preparedness in response to COVID-19. The respondent's comments on shortages (Clue 2) indicate systemic failures that hinder effective care. The mention of reduced drug production due to workforce layoffs connects the pandemic's economic impacts to health service constraints (Clue 3). Additionally, references to ambulance service inefficiencies and prior border restrictions illustrate challenges in operational response. Overall, the clues reflect significant gaps in the health system's capacity to manage the pandemic effectively.

Reasoning (max 150 words): The clues reveal significant challenges in resource allocation and supply chain management within the health system. The respondent's statements regarding drug scarcity (Clue 1) highlight the acute shortages affecting service delivery. The mention of increased living costs suggests broader economic impacts from the pandemic, straining supply chains (Clue 1). The inadequate supply of essential medications, such as ACT (Clue 3), emphasizes systemic failures exacerbated by the pandemic.
